title: Taifa of Granada
capsule: The Taifa of Granada was an independent Muslim principality in southern Iberia ruled by the Berber Zirid dynasty, which seized autonomous control of the city around 1013–1015 following the collapse of the Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba. It reached its greatest extent and cultural prominence under Badis ibn Habus (r. 1038–1073), whose Jewish viziers Samuel ibn Naghrila and his son Joseph wielded substantial administrative power; Joseph was killed in a pogrom in 1066. The Almoravid sultan Yusuf ibn Tashfin annexed Granada in 1090, ending the Zirid line and incorporating the taifa into the North African empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political boundaries of this taifa are moderately well documented through Arabic chronicles such as Ibn Idhari's al-Bayan al-Mughrib, though precise territorial extents fluctuated and are difficult to map with precision.
